readerQuestion: Should I run one Home Assistant server for two separate properties, or install one independent server in each home?
selectedBecause: The same one-server-or-separate-servers decision recurs in current r/homeassistant and Home Assistant Community discussions from people adding a vacation home, workshop, office, or second household. The exact Google results remain split among forum answers, Companion app setup, Cloud account policy, and administrator-oriented fleet material instead of giving a plain homeowner architecture guide. The answer is durable and consequential because it affects whether local devices and automations depend on a cross-site internet or VPN connection. Tara has relevant articles about remote access, outages, backups, and moving hardware, but no page owns multi-property design. Search Console's current high-impression queries already belong to other owner paths and contain no close variation of this question, so this topic adds coverage without splitting an existing URL's intent.

demandSignals.evidence: The exact query returns community threads, Companion app fragments, a Cloud account FAQ, and multi-instance administration material, but no leading result gives a homeowner a complete one-server-versus-one-per-property decision with outage and local-radio consequences.

A current second-home discussion asks how two locations appear in the app and how notifications behave. Replies describe separate local installations, multiple-server app access, separate Cloud accounts, and optional community linking.

A separate home-and-workshop question asks whether to use one installation across town or keep both locations independent. The recurring answer favors one local controller per site so basic operation does not depend on the internet.

The current community discussion revisits the same architecture decision for two homes and weighs centralized convenience against separate local control, showing that the question persists even as remote networking becomes easier.

Another independently active discussion compares centralized and site-local installations for multiple properties, including network-failure behavior and the management tradeoff rather than a one-off setup symptom.

The Home Assistant architecture discussion records long-running demand to link separate installations, including a house and holiday home, and explains why site-local automation resilience matters when the connection between properties fails.

searchReview.intent: The searcher wants to decide whether distant properties should share one Home Assistant installation or use one server at each site, then learn how to reach both from a phone and what the choice means during an internet outage.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results divide the answer among a fleet-management comparison, community recommendations, Companion app instructions, an old multi-server app announcement, and a narrow Cloud subscription FAQ. They do not present one homeowner-friendly decision that covers physically separate properties versus same-LAN outbuildings, Zigbee and Z-Wave radio locality, cross-site connection failures, app switching, remote access, subscriptions, separate backups, and the unofficial status of cross-instance aggregation.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Companion: Getting started
officialSources.supports: The official Companion app can add additional Home Assistant servers from Settings, discover servers on the same network, or accept a server URL manually.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Companion: Sensors
officialSources.supports: With multiple servers connected, phone sensors can be sent on a per-server basis, while some sensor settings remain common across the connected servers.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Companion: URL handler
officialSources.supports: Official deep links have multiple-server behavior that should be considered when a notification or shortcut is meant to open a particular property's dashboard.

officialSources.name: Nabu Casa: Multiple Home Assistant installations
officialSources.supports: Each installation using Home Assistant Cloud needs its own account and subscription; reusing one account across installations causes unpredictable service and leaves only one installation active.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant: Remote access
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant documents Cloud as the easiest secure remote-access path, lists VPN as an alternative, and warns that simply exposing a port is not secure.

existingCoverage.decision: No current Tara page owns the choice between one Home Assistant server across multiple properties and one independent server per site. The outage article owns failure behavior, the remote-access article owns safe off-site access, the backup and migration articles own recovery and hardware moves, and /local-smart-home-hub/ owns the commercial hub decision. The new article will answer only the multi-property architecture and management question, link to those pages descriptively, and keep the commercial recommendation on its existing owner path.
